title: Wattuquasset (Lake Montauk)
summary: Wattuquasset is a small neck on the southwest side of Great Pond at Montauk, now Lake Montauk.
history_content: The neck belongs to the Montauk pond-and-neck landscape where haystacks and other landmarks served as boundary references. The dated deed is handled as a Timeline Entry.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as at or near the poles, probably referring to haystack poles or a related landmark.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names may have many levels of meaning, and multiple stories attached to them.”

— Rachel Mason and Eileen Devinney, Alaska Native Place Names in Arctic Parks (2017), final paragraph
preservation_content: Wattuquasset preserves a small-place name from the Montauk landscape around Great Pond, where working landmarks and deed boundaries overlapped.
whereintheworld_content: Blue/general approximate marker on the southwest side of Lake Montauk. This is not an exact 1683 deed-boundary coordinate.
